findings.title: updateDevice uses ? placeholders on all DB types, breaks Postgres
findings.body: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go updateDevice builds UPDATE with ? placeholders for all drivers. CreateOrUpdateDevice right below switches on GetDBType and uses $1..$5 for Postgres because Postgres does not accept ?. updateDevice has no such switch, so on Postgres the Exec will fail with syntax error when the device limit is reached, meaning limit enforcement is broken on Postgres.

findings.title: Device cache set before DB write lets rejected devices bypass limit on retry
findings.body: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go tagDeviceUI does localCache.SetDefault(key) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and never removes it on error. If CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the cache entry for that new deviceID remains. The next Authenticate with the same deviceID hits the cache in tagDeviceUI and returns nil, so authentication succeeds without a DB row. An attacker denied once can retry with the same ID to bypass the limit.

findings.title: Count-then-insert check is not atomic, limit can be exceeded
findings.body: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go CreateOrUpdateDevice does CountDevices then, if count >= limit, update-only else unconditional INSERT/UPSERT in separate sessions/transactions. Concurrent anonymous logins can both observe count < limit and both insert, exceeding the configured deviceLimit. There is no transaction, lock, or unique-count constraint to make the check atomic.

findings.title: Expired existing device cannot re-activate once limit is reached
findings.body: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go updateDevice requires updated_at BETWEEN now-30d AND now+1m and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected==0. CountDevices only counts rows in that same active window, so a device whose row expired (>30d old) is not counted but its update also matches 0 rows and is rejected as over-limit. A returning stale device can never refresh its row while at limit, permanently locking it out.

findings.title: Anonymous auth changed from async fire-and-forget to synchronous DB writes
findings.body: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go Authenticate previously tagged the device in a background goroutine with its own timeout so login never waited on the anon_device table. It now calls TagDevice synchronously on the request context, which when deviceLimit>0 adds a SELECT COUNT(*) plus INSERT/UPDATE to the critical auth path of every anonymous request. This adds latency, DB load, and couples login availability to the anon store; request cancellation also cancels tagging.

findings.title: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService breaks DI by replacing AnonStore with db.DB
findings.body: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go ProvideAnonymousDeviceService changed its parameter from anonstore.AnonStore to db.DB and now constructs the store internally via ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit). Callers, wire injectors, and tests that injected a mock/fake AnonStore can no longer do so, and the service cannot be unit-tested without a real DB. The constructor should keep accepting the interface and pass the limit separately.
